result.title: SPARC: Geometry-Guided Attention Pruning for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation
result.summary: We present SPARC, a geometry-guided attention pruning framework that turns the native self-attention of pretrained video diffusion transformers into a unified mechanism for camera control and persistent scene memory. Our key insight is that attention connectivity can simultaneously serve as geometric conditioning for camera control and spatial addressing for historical memory retrieval. Motivated by the asymmetric contextual requirements of reconstructing observed content and synthesizing novel regions, SPARC restricts observed tokens to geometrically corresponding historical tokens and local spatiotemporal context, while preserving dense attention for unobserved regions. Correspondence-aware attention biasing and order-invariant historical positioning further enable stable retrieval across long temporal gaps. Without introducing additional learnable control or memory modules, SPARC achieves precise camera adherence and faithful scene revisitation while substantially reducing attention computation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of aggressive attention pruning in improving camera adherence, revisit consistency, and visual fidelity, with an inference speedup of over 50x when combined with four-step distillation. Project page is available at https://zju3dv.github.io/SPARC.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SPARC，把预训练视频扩散 Transformer 的自注意力改作相机控制与持久场景记忆的统一机制：对已观测 token 仅保留几何对应的历史 token 与局部时空上下文，未观测区域保持稠密注意力，从而在不加控制或记忆模块的前提下减少注意力计算。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以注意力连通性充当空间寻址、按几何对应筛选历史 token 并做顺序无关定位」的做法，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、历史缓存访问与注意力结构分析提供方法线索；但论文属视频生成场景，迁移可行性需核查。
